title: path
lede: Node's `path` module for portable filesystem path manipulation, import-gated as a virtual built-in (`import path from 'path'`). The whole module is POSIX-only — this compiler doesn't cross-compile, so `sep` is always `/` and `delimiter` always `:`, and no Windows `\`/`;` forms are ever emitted. Everything else — join, resolve, dirname, basename, extname, parse/format, isAbsolute — matches real Node's algorithms, including its asymmetric `basename` extension-stripping rule.

entries.name: path.join(...segments)
entries.description: Joins segments with `/`, then normalizes the result: collapses repeated slashes, drops `.` segments, and resolves `..` against segments already seen in the same call.

entries.name: path.resolve(...segments)
entries.description: Absolute-always: starts from `process.cwd()`, walks segments left to right, any segment starting with `/` resets the accumulator (discarding everything before it, including cwd) — equivalent to real Node's right-to-left "stop at the last absolute segment" algorithm.

entries.name: path.dirname(p)
entries.description: Directory portion of a path; trailing slashes are trimmed first.

entries.name: path.basename(p, ext?)
entries.description: Final path segment, optionally with a trailing `ext` stripped — not stripped when doing so would consume the whole segment, unless the entire `path` argument equals `ext` (then returns `""`), matching real Node's own asymmetric rule here.

entries.name: path.extname(p)
entries.description: Extension of the basename, including the leading `.`; returns `""` for a dotfile whose only `.` is its first character.

entries.name: path.parse(p) / path.format(obj)
entries.signature: parse(p: string): { root, dir, base, ext, name }; format(obj): string
entries.description: `parse` returns `{root, dir, base, ext, name}`; `format` is the inverse (`base` wins over `name`+`ext`, `dir` falls back to `root`).

returns.desc: A parsed path object, or a reassembled string.

entries.name: path.isAbsolute(p)
entries.description: True when the path is absolute — `p[0] === '/'`.

entries.name: path.sep / path.delimiter
entries.description: The path-segment separator and the PATH-style delimiter, as compile-time constants.
differences: POSIX-only (this compiler doesn't cross-compile) — the compile-time constants `/` and `:`, never the Windows `\`/`;` forms
